description: Formal contract for apps/phantom-guard: the cloud audit event schema, the resource discovery rules (orphaned EBS volumes, zombie EC2/RDS instances, idle NAT gateways), the audit decision model, the Terraform plan scanner and the TTL eviction rules. Every clause carries an implementation status ('implemented', 'partial' or 'planned') so the contract is honest about what the code does at this commit. Binding rules live in .kiro/steering/architecture.md; where this file and template.yaml disagree, template.yaml wins.
rules: Buffer AWS CloudTrail & EventBridge alerts through AegisIngestionQueue.
Trigger automatic circuit breaking on unbudgeted EC2/RDS resource spikes.
Store audit trails in DynamoDB Pay-Per-Request.

eventSchema.title: PhantomGuard cloud audit event
eventSchema.description: Envelope accepted by POST /ingest and delivered through SQS. A CloudTrail or EventBridge event is normalised by the producer into this shape; the sentry does not parse raw CloudTrail records. Unknown fields are carried but ignored.

id.description: Idempotency identifier of the message. Used as the resource key when payload.resource_id is absent.

resource_id.description: Provider identifier, e.g. i-0abc123, vol-0def456, a DB instance identifier. Becomes SK = RESOURCE#<resource_id>. 255 characters at up to 4 bytes each plus the 9-byte prefix stays under the 1024-byte DynamoDB sort-key limit.

resource_type.description: CloudFormation-style resource type. The circuit breaker keys on the exact strings AWS::EC2::Instance and AWS::RDS::DBInstance.

cost_per_hour.description: Estimated hourly cost in USD. Producers must send a decimal string (or an integer). A JSON number with a fractional part is rejected because it was almost certainly produced by binary floating point (Rule 4). The core stores it as a two-decimal string, so sub-cent hourly rates are rounded to cents.

state.description: EBS volume state as reported by EC2 (DescribeVolumes). 'available' means the volume is not attached. Read by discovery rule DR-1.

attachments.description: EBS volume attachments (DescribeVolumes) or Terraform 'attachments'. An empty array means unattached; absent means unknown and is never treated as unattached. Read by discovery rule DR-1.

observed_at.description: Epoch seconds at which the producer observed the resource. Reserved for rule DR-2 'sustained' checks.

resourceDiscoveryRules.name: orphaned-ebs-volume
resourceDiscoveryRules.condition: state == 'available' OR attachments is an empty array
resourceDiscoveryRules.rationale: An unattached EBS volume bills for its provisioned size every hour and serves nothing. Example: fixtures/tfplan.json declares a 100 GB gp3 volume with attachments [].

decision.remediation: Snapshot if needed, then delete the volume.

resourceDiscoveryRules.notes: An event carrying neither attachments nor state is ALLOWed: the sentry never invents unattachment. Plan-level scanning prices the orphan with the gp3/gp2 list price in Decimal; an unpriced volume type is still flagged, without a monetary estimate.

resourceDiscoveryRules.name: zombie-ec2-rds
resourceDiscoveryRules.rationale: AegisSkeleton is zero-idle: no always-on EC2 or RDS may exist (steering Rule 3). Any such resource reaching the sentry is unbudgeted by definition and trips the circuit breaker.
resourceDiscoveryRules.caveat: The decision is recorded only. The sentry calls no EC2 or RDS API, so nothing is terminated: 'TERMINATE_SIGNAL_SENT' is a label on the audit row. The match is on resource_type alone, with no budget, age or utilisation check, so a legitimate instance and a zombie are indistinguishable.

resourceDiscoveryRules.name: idle-nat-gateway
resourceDiscoveryRules.rationale: A NAT gateway bills a flat hourly charge ($0.045/hr in us-east-1) whether or not traffic flows, so it is planned idle burn in a scale-to-zero stack. Data-processing GB is not declared in a Terraform plan and is therefore never priced.

decision.remediation: Review the route tables; replace with a VPC endpoint where the traffic is S3 / DynamoDB.

resourceDiscoveryRules.notes: Plan scan: hourly = $0.045, monthly = hourly x 730, both decimal strings from ROUND_HALF_UP.

decisionModel.description: One audit event yields one decision stored on the resource row. Rules are evaluated in order and the first match wins; an event that matches no rule is allowed.

persistence.writeSemantics: PutItem, last write wins: one row per resource holding its most recent audit decision. There is no per-event history.

writers.role: canonical writer; normalises estimated_hourly_burn to a two-decimal string and sets resource_id and ttl

domain writer; writes the same key first, so a domain event costs two writes. Without payload.resource_id it writes SK = RESOURCE#UNIDENTIFIED and omits the resource_id attribute, so the core falls back to the SQS envelope id instead of storing a None row.

accessPatterns.name: list tripped breakers
accessPatterns.notes: No GSI by design (Rule 2). The filter runs after the read, so it does not reduce consumed read units.

itemSchema.title: PhantomGuard audit item (as stored in AegisStateTable)

estimated_hourly_burn.description: str(Decimal), two places, ROUND_HALF_UP. Sub-cent hourly rates are rounded: 0.0416 is stored as 0.04.

audited_at.description: Epoch seconds when the sentry evaluated the event. ttl = audited_at + 86400, give or take the second boundary between the two clock reads.

ttl.description: Epoch seconds, written on every item (Rule 2).

ttlEviction.formula: ttl = int(time.time()) + 86400, written on every PutItem

rules.statement: Every audit row carries ttl. A row without ttl is unbounded storage and is a hard failure.
The TTL budget is 86400 seconds. Changing it requires amending .kiro/steering/architecture.md in the same commit.

A new audit event for the same resource overwrites the row and restarts the 24 hour window. A resource that keeps reporting never expires; a resource that stops reporting disappears 24 hours after its last event.
DynamoDB deletes expired items asynchronously, typically some hours after expiry. Readers must filter on ttl > now and must not assume an expired row is already gone.
The audit trail is a rolling 24 hour view of current resource state, not a permanent record. Anything that must outlive 24 hours has to be exported elsewhere before expiry.

planScanner.transport: MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio; identical frame, tool-result and error-code contract to mcp/aegis_mcp_server.py
planScanner.input: fixtures/tfplan.json by default, or an inline decoded plan; repository-relative paths only
planScanner.money: decimal.Decimal, quantized to 6 dp with ROUND_HALF_UP; every figure is emitted as a string
planScanner.fixtureVerdict: 4 resources scanned, 2 flagged (orphaned 100 GB gp3 volume, idle provisioned concurrency), $62.750438/month and $753.005256/year

knownDeviations: TERMINATE_SIGNAL_SENT is a label: the sentry makes no EC2 or RDS API call, so no resource is terminated.
The domain writer stores the hourly burn with six decimals; the canonical core writer re-quantises it to two decimals, so sub-cent burn is rounded to cents on the persisted row (0.0416 becomes 0.04).

Plan scanning (mcp/finops_sentry.py) prices only list rates declared in that module; NAT data-processing GB, provisioned IOPS and instance-type rates are not in a Terraform plan and are reported as flagged-but-unpriced.
A payload without resource_id still produces a domain row at SK = RESOURCE#UNIDENTIFIED before the core writes SK = RESOURCE#<envelope id>; the two writes are not atomic.
